gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate NAS costs to run around the clock. For a Frigate box this is the figure that matters, because continuous recording keeps the disks spinning, so only the drive-access wattage counts. At the August 2026 US average rate (18.16 ¢/kWh) that ranges from about $26 a year (UGREEN DXP2800, 16.38 W) to about $72 a year (TerraMaster F4-425 Plus, 45.0 W maker spec).
standout_why: Compared against docs.frigate.video/frigate/hardware (cited in every chat) and our current dealectric.com page. The Frigate page gives detector inference times and names mini PCs, but it has no wattage, no running cost and no NAS models. Our page lists CPU, RAM, detector options, Docker route, warranty and price, and has no power or electricity figure at all. ChatGPT's answers give storage TB per camera and nothing on power. None of them points out that the hibernation wattage NAS makers advertise does not apply when the NAS records 24/7.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. The DXP4800 Plus at $619.99 measured 24.25 W idle with drives spinning (KitGuru), about $39 a year. The three other 4-bay x86 candidates are rated by their makers at 37.9–45.0 W in drive access, about $60–72 a year. Over five years that is roughly $110–165 more on the electricity bill, which more than covers the F4-425 Plus's $80 lower price today. Caveat: KitGuru's DXP4800 Plus number is a measured idle figure and the others are maker access ratings, so the like-for-like comparison is among the maker-rated models only. Among 2-bay boxes for 1–4 cameras, the DXP2800 (16.38 W, $389.99) and DS225+ (16.98 W) cost about the same to run. The AS5402T (22.9 W) costs about $10 more a year.
